article.headline: England storms to series win as Ben Duckett routs Australia in Hobart
article.summary: Ben Duckett and Sonny Baker led England to a 97-run victory over Australia on Wednesday to secure a 2-1 series win.
article.body:
Ben Duckett hammered 133 runs to anchor England's total, setting the stage for a dominant bowling performance that silenced the home crowd in Hobart. While Australia sought to defend its territory, the visitors surged to a massive 328 all out, proving too formidable for the Australian lineup during the final showdown of the series.

This victory marks a definitive turnaround for the English side, which began the contest trailing 1-0 after initial struggles. By overcoming that early deficit, the team demonstrated remarkable resilience, successfully flipping the script after their emphatic 135-run win in Adelaide last Sunday. For fans and observers, the result solidifies England's current momentum in the international cricket format.

The final match saw Australia crumble to 231 all out as England’s pace attack dictated the pace of play. Pace bowler Sonny Baker proved instrumental, dismantling the batting order with four crucial wickets, while teammate Liam Dawson chipped in with another three wickets. Ben Duckett’s century remained the defining offensive effort of the day, ensuring England’s total remained out of reach for the hosts throughout the final innings.

The series concludes with England walking away as winners, having successfully weathered a challenging start to turn the tide across the three-match series. The clinical performance in Hobart confirms the visitors' dominance in the deciding fixture, leaving Australia unable to respond to the relentless pressure applied by the English bowlers and Duckett’s high-scoring display at the crease.

article.headline: S&P 500 Plunges Into Correction Territory as AI Investment Fervor Cools Down
article.summary: The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 10% from recent highs by Friday, signaling a market correction.
article.body:
The benchmark S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average have officially retreated into correction territory, marking a decline of more than 10% from their most recent peaks. This sharp downturn arrived as the broader market struggled to absorb mounting anxiety regarding the sustainability of artificial intelligence stocks, which have faced intense scrutiny due to regulatory hurdles and significant reported financial losses. The reversal represents a stark contrast to previous growth trends as investors rapidly retreat from high-exposure AI positions.

This shift in sentiment signals a broader cooling of the tech-driven optimism that defined the market earlier in the year. The loss of confidence among institutional and retail investors suggests that the massive capital inflows into AI companies are now facing a reality check, with the market demanding concrete proof of profitability over speculative hype. For those with exposure to major indexes or tech-heavy portfolios, this period marks a pivot from aggressive growth to defensive caution.

Adding to the downward pressure, the Nasdaq composite has completely erased its gains for the year. According to CNN, the highly anticipated initial public offering of Anthropic failed to act as a stabilizing force, doing little to ease the nerves of investors worried about the long-term viability of the sector. The combination of regulatory concerns and missed earnings expectations has left the tech industry vulnerable to heavy sell-offs, dragging the wider market down with it.

Analysts are now monitoring market performance to see if indices can find a new floor or if the current momentum will lead to further volatility in the coming weeks. The failure of recent market catalysts to ignite a rally suggests that investor caution will likely persist as financial markets digest the current downturn.

The Guardian reports that Manchester City enters this clash aiming to correct their downward trajectory in the league following an international break. article.headline: Bayern Munich loses Harry Kane for months following Cologne Bundesliga draw
article.summary: Bayern Munich and Cologne drew 1-1 in Friday's Bundesliga match, with Harry Kane suffering a syndesmosis ankle ligament injury.
article.body:
Harry Kane was forced off in the 20th minute of Friday night's Bundesliga match after suffering a tear to the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle. Club official Eberl and manager Vincent Kompany confirmed after the final whistle that the striker now faces a recovery period of several months. The injury occurred during a 1-1 draw against Cologne, adding to an extensive list of sidelined players for the German champions including Manuel Neuer, Alphonso Davies, and Serge Gnabry.

The loss of Kane, who was replaced by Tom Bischof early in the first half, presents a significant hurdle for Kompany. The manager had just returned to the dugout following a month-long absence due to illness. With key players like Michael Olise also exiting the match with a bruised foot and Jamal Musiala causing concern, Bayern's depth is being severely tested as they navigate a dense schedule. The draw leaves Bayern at 22 points, holding a one-point lead over Borussia Dortmund, who have the opportunity to move to the top of the table on Saturday.

Mikey Moore provided the opening goal for Cologne in the 12th minute following an assist by Said El Mala. Nathaniel Brown secured the equalizer for Bayern in the 37th minute after a setup from the substitute Bischof. Despite substitutions in the 70th minute bringing on Musiala and Kim Min-Jae, the score remained level until the final whistle.

Bayern now shifts focus to European competition. They are scheduled to travel to France to face Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday 25 November. Following that, they return to domestic league action with an away fixture in Hamburg on Saturday 28 November.

article.headline: Colts dump Daniel Jones as Anthony Richardson takes over starting role
article.summary: The Indianapolis Colts waived quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday and named Anthony Richardson their new starter following a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans.
article.body:
The Indianapolis Colts terminated Daniel Jones' contract Friday, just hours after a lackluster performance in a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Jones, who completed only 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and an interception during the game, ended his 11-game stint with the team while leading the league with 13 interceptions. Coach Shane Steichen, who had defended the quarterback earlier in the week, ultimately benched him in the fourth quarter before confirming the release was in the best interest of both sides.

This decision forces an immediate shift for opposing teams, including the New York Giants. Giants coach John Harbaugh admitted that the news blindsided his staff, who were already preparing scouting reports for a matchup against an Indianapolis team led by Jones. Because Anthony Richardson brings a vastly different style of play to the position, New York's coaches must now scrap their existing film study and prepare for Richardson’s first start in two years, scheduled for November 29.

According to NFL Network, Jones remains on waivers until Monday at 4 p.m. ET. Any team that claims him inherits the remainder of his contract, which includes just over $2 million for the current season and $38 million in non-guaranteed money for 2027. Despite his struggles, coach Steichen praised Jones' competitiveness, noting the quarterback’s efforts to play through injuries including a broken leg and a torn Achilles during his time with the organization.

The Colts, currently sitting at 3-8, are now fully pivoting to Richardson for the remainder of the season. Richardson made a brief appearance in the final minutes of the loss to Houston, and he is expected to be the focal point of the offense moving forward as the team attempts to reset following the departure of their high-priced veteran.

article.headline: S&P 500 and Dow Jones plunge into official 10% market correction
article.summary: U.S. indices hit correction territory on Friday as a tech-driven sell-off wiped out Nasdaq gains for 2026.
article.body:
Nvidia shares plummeted 14% on Friday alone, bringing the chipmaker's total loss for the month of November to nearly 40%. The selling pressure intensified following reports of a Securities and Exchange Commission probe into the company’s accounting, while the recent resignation of CEO Jensen Huang amid an affair with an alleged Chinese spy further rattled investor confidence. This decline marks a significant shift for a stock that until recently served as the primary engine for the artificial intelligence bull market.

The broader market correction, defined as a decline of at least 10% from record highs, reflects deepening anxiety regarding the sustainability of the AI trade. Analysts compare the current wave of fear to the volatility observed during the Covid-19 pandemic. The Nasdaq index alone suffered its worst performance in a single week since March 2020, dropping 10% as investors questioned the high valuations and massive capital expenditures of major AI-focused companies.

Adding to the market turbulence was the high-profile IPO of Anthropic. After debuting Thursday at $83 and surging above $115, the stock immediately reversed course and closed Friday at $88.91. This sharp swing reinforced investor fears that recent large-scale public offerings represent a collective cash-out by early players in the AI complex. While tech stocks led the downturn, the sell-off extended to broader indices, with the S&P 500 falling 3.7% and the Dow Jones industrial average dropping 1.93% during Friday’s trading session.

The pressure was not limited to U.S. exchanges, as the S&P/TSX composite index in Canada also slipped into correction territory after a 2.47% single-day decline. With the Nasdaq having erased all of its gains accumulated throughout 2026, market participants are now bracing for continued volatility as the reality of the AI-led rally faces its most severe test to date.

article.headline: England steamrolls All Blacks as 37-12 victory sets record-breaking misery for visitors
article.summary: England secured a decisive 37-12 Nations Championship victory over New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, marking a record loss for the All Blacks.
article.body:
The 80,000 spectators at Twickenham witnessed a one-way fight as England recorded its largest-ever win against the All Blacks, eclipsing the 2012 result of 38-21. This defeat marks the fifth loss for New Zealand this season, matching the worst record in their professional era, a tally not seen since the 1998 season. England, now riding a five-match unbeaten run, physically dominated the breakdowns and forced 16 turnovers from the visitors throughout the contest.

For the All Blacks, the result represents a significant setback in their recent campaign, coming immediately after a historic loss to Wales. The team struggled to maintain momentum, suffering from a failing lineout and a defense that conceded 12 clean breaks. As reported by the NZ Herald, the visitors appeared flat and lethargic against a hungry England side, unable to execute a cohesive attacking platform. 

England captain Maro Itoje praised his squad’s rapid start and the impact provided by the bench players in his post-match comments to ITV. The victory cements England’s current form in the Nations Championship and further exposes the ongoing struggles of the All Blacks under Dave Rennie. The result marks the first time New Zealand has lost to England twice in consecutive visits to Twickenham since the 2002-2003 era.

While the Nations Championship rankings continue, the team now looks toward next week's fixtures to maintain their momentum. England remains focused on sustaining their current level of performance, with Itoje emphasizing that the team is only as good as their next game.

article.summary: The Springboks prepare for their Nations Championship Test against Ireland in Dublin without head coach Rassie Erasmus following his six-match suspension for criticizing officials.
article.body:
Rassie Erasmus will watch Saturday's match from his team's Dublin hotel, barred from all contact with his players and management due to a suspension for questioning the integrity of referee Andrea Piardi and television match official Matteo Liperini. The ban followed the Springboks' recent defeat in Paris, a game that also saw back row Jasper Wiese suspended for four matches following a dangerous ruck clearout. 

This high-stakes fixture at the Aviva Stadium has become a focal point of the November rugby schedule, testing the team's resilience after a turbulent week. Assistant coach Mzwandile Stick remains defiant, stating that the squad feels in a good space and that no external pressure will break the team. The importance of the match extends beyond the pitch, as captain Siya Kolisi emphasized that the players carry the weight of national expectation every time they represent South Africa. 

According to the BBC, Erasmus remains a two-time World Cup winner despite the controversy surrounding his recent conduct. The team looks to move past the disciplinary fallout by focusing on their performance on the field against Ireland, aiming to channel the expectations of their supporters back home into a victory. This match continues a series of must-see events in the current Nations Championship, with the focus now shifting entirely to the players and the remaining coaching staff who must navigate the game without their head coach present.

article.headline: Breezy Conditions and Scattered Showers Sweep Across Hawaii Islands This Saturday
article.summary: Maui and Hawaii County face varying weather patterns this weekend with high chances of rain and persistent winds expected across multiple regions.
article.body:
Residents across Hawaii can expect a weekend dominated by breezy conditions and varying chances of precipitation, as isolated to numerous showers are forecasted to move through the islands. In Maui, the weather outlook for Saturday calls for widespread breezy conditions, with some areas seeing mostly sunny skies while others remain mostly cloudy with up to a 70 percent chance of rain in certain districts. Summit areas, such as the visitor center, will see temperatures ranging from roughly 42 to 65 degrees, accompanied by consistent east winds blowing between 15 and 25 mph. 

Understanding these shifts is vital for planning outdoor weekend activities, particularly for those living near the shore or in higher elevations where temperatures and rainfall probabilities differ significantly. The impact of these winds and localized rain showers will dictate daily routines, especially in areas where the chance of precipitation climbs as high as 70 percent throughout the day. 

According to reports from Maui Now, the island will experience breezy conditions with intermittent sun and clouds. Meanwhile, Big Island Now indicates that Hawaii County is bracing for a mix of sunny periods and likely showers, particularly in the morning. Regions in Hawaii County should anticipate northeast winds of up to 15 mph, with rain chances fluctuating between 20 and 90 percent depending on the specific location and elevation. 

As the weekend progresses, travelers and residents are encouraged to monitor local updates for any rapid changes in wind speeds or precipitation levels. These weather patterns are typical for this time of year, with breezy winds continuing to influence both temperatures and shower frequency across the archipelago through Saturday night.

article.summary: Galatasaray faces Samsunspor at NEF Stadyumu as the league leaders aim to build on their 28-point total.
article.body: Galatasaray enters the clash with a formidable record, boasting six consecutive wins across all competitions. This run includes high-profile victories such as a 2-1 derby win against Fenerbahçe and Champions League triumphs over VfB Stuttgart and Lille. Okan Buruk’s squad has been clinical, scoring 13 goals while conceding only four in their last five competitive appearances, including a recent 4-3 Süper Lig victory over Amed Sportif.  For Samsunspor, the match represents a critical battle for survival as the team sits second from the bottom of the table. Coach Nenad Bjelica’s side has struggled significantly, losing four of their last five league matches. Their recent defensive woes were highlighted by a 5-2 defeat to Istanbul Basaksehir, and they have conceded 14 goals over their last four winless games.  The contrast between the two clubs is stark, with Galatasaray maintaining their position as clear league leaders with 28 points. While the club manages its roster, midfielder Ilkay Gündogan has publicly confirmed he will remain with Galatasaray through the winter despite limited playing time, expressing his commitment to winning titles with the team following his arrival in September 2025.  The Süper Lig match takes place at NEF Stadyumu in Istanbul. Fans will be watching to see if the league leaders can further widen the gap at the top of the table or if Samsunspor can secure a much-needed result to improve their standing in the league.

article.headline: Happy Days Star Henry Winkler Rushed to Ennis Hospital After Gout Scare
article.summary: Actor Henry Winkler was treated at an Ennis emergency department on Thursday following a painful gout flare-up during his Irish tour.
article.body:
Henry Winkler, globally recognized for his iconic role as Arthur 'The Fonz' Fonzarelli, experienced an unexpected health setback while vacationing in Ireland. The 81-year-old actor revealed that a dietary decision to consume excess cheese led to an acute bout of gout, necessitating an urgent visit to an A+E department in Ennis on Thursday. Despite the pain, Winkler expressed sincere gratitude to the medical staff who provided care during his time of need.

Following his hospital visit, the Emmy-winning performer highlighted the hospitality of local emergency responders. During an appearance on the Late Late Show, Winkler shared that he was later lifted into the air by the Dublin Fire Brigade using a basket, a gesture he described as fantastic. This visit is part of a broader tour of Ireland that has taken the actor through locations including Kinsale, the Rock of Cashel, and the English Market in Cork.

Reporting on his experiences, RTE noted that Winkler is currently visiting the country ahead of his scheduled appearance at Comic Con Ireland 2026. This trip marks the latest in a series of memorable Irish visits for the actor, who previously gained notice during a hotel fire drill evacuation in a prior year. Beyond his television legacy, Winkler continues his active career, with his latest film project, Hexed, set to arrive in cinemas next week.

Looking ahead, the star is set to appear before fans at the RDS in Dublin this weekend for Comic Con. His account of his recent health emergency provided a lighthearted moment during his scheduled promotional tour stops, balancing his professional commitments with his personal travels across the region.

article.headline: Nvidia Shares Plunge as SEC Investigation Adds to $2.7 Trillion Market Rout
article.summary: Nvidia stock fell nearly 14% on Friday amid a reported SEC investigation into the company's accounting practices.
article.body:
Nvidia has shed roughly $2.7 trillion in market value since its October 6 peak, with Friday’s 14% single-day collapse marking its worst performance since January 2025. This historic decline left the former world’s most valuable company ranked fourth in the U.S. market, trailing behind Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet.

For investors, the uncertainty surrounding the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) probe compounds a week of heavy losses. While an investigation does not confirm fraud or guarantee enforcement, the scrutiny into accounting practices arrives as federal authorities also examine chip export rule compliance and previous leadership changes. The financial impact is significant, with the company losing nearly $900 billion in market capitalization over the past week alone.

According to The Motley Fool and Yahoo Finance, the SEC is investigating potential accounting irregularities, with reports from The Wall Street Journal noting questions over whether disclosures misled investors. Specific focus areas may include how Nvidia records geographic revenue and its relationship with customers like Singapore-based Megaspeed, which officials suspect of rerouting chips to China. Additionally, Nvidia has reported longer collection times, with outstanding bills reaching 64 days of sales, the longest duration since 2022.

The pressure on the company is mounting from Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has publicly requested answers from the board and outside counsel within 10 days regarding the internal situation. Nvidia has also delayed its 10-Q filing, opting to release the detailed quarterly report in the coming weeks while an independent board committee conducts its own ongoing investigation.

news.title: Weekend Plans With ‘Frasier’ Star Kelsey Grammer
news.og_title: Weekend Plans With ‘Frasier’ Star Kelsey Grammer
news.og_desc: Weekend Plans is our exclusive lifestyle feature where we highlight the real off-duty routines of the most exciting people in culture. This weekend, Kelsey Grammer — the acclaimed actor behind psychiatrist Dr. Frasier Crane on “Frasier” and “Cheers” — chats with The Daily Wire about his new coffee table book “The America Opus,” the ’70s thriller that nearly scarred him for life, the seminal works he draws on daily, and how this former surfer teen turned unlikely odds into a shining example of the American dream. ***If you were wondering how similar Kelsey Grammer is to the character he made famous, we were already discussing world-renowned opera singer Plácido Domingo just minutes into our chat. I grew up watching “Frasier,” and my parents quote the show all the time. “Even we quote it sometimes,” Kelsey says with a smile. I have no proof, but I think my IQ rose a point just because of this. He recalls a scene from season 11 that he filmed with the late Sir Patrick Stewart. “I was working with [Patrick] last year … and I told him I’ve been writing some stuff, and he said, ‘Oh yeah, I hope you’re not writing about me.’ Well, I actually was,” Kelsey says. “I wrote about how there was a scene when Niles and Frasier met this opera director — who was Patrick Stewart — and he’s on the phone. He says, ‘Plácido,’ and then Niles and Frasier go, ‘Plácido Domingo.’ We do that all the time in my house.”Having starred in several pop-culture behemoths (he also voices Sideshow Bob on “The Simpsons”), Kelsey’s been a recognizable face in entertainment since the ’80s. But he won’t succumb to the whim of every fan just to stay relevant. “I don’t really do much for my fans, honestly. Except field really strange requests,” he says after I warn him we’ll be going behind the scenes, so to speak. Alluding to oddball demands of fan texts, he adds, “I don’t even know who any of these people are. I just keep blocking them or reporting it as spam. Then somebody else shows up. You think, how is this possible?”We briefly joke that he could be making a lot of money answering these types of requests on another platform that shall remain nameless. But he’s carved out a lauded career without relying on easy cash grabs, all while defying the odds.Kelsey faced tragedy early in his life when his father Frank was murdered. Several years later, his sister Karen suffered a similar fate. Somewhere in between navigating waves of grief as a teen surfer in Florida, Kelsey gained acceptance into the prestigious Juilliard School in New York City to study drama on not much more than a whim.“I was a surfer and I sang in churches,” Kelsey explains. After acting in a play in 11th grade (“The Little Foxes” by Lillian Hellman), he remembers, “It was actually a pretty good play and I was good in it. I thought to myself, well, I could do this the rest of my life.”He enrolled in music camp at Florida State University that summer, and when he was asked by his high school counselor what he wanted to do, Kelsey told him, “I think I wanna give this acting thing a shot. I said, ‘I hear Juilliard is the best school in America, and then I heard Carnegie Mellon’s right up there too, so I’m gonna apply to them.’”Just Juilliard, where the acceptance rate is famously in the single digits. “I was too stupid to be intimidated,” Kelsey laughs. He recalls British actor and producer John Houseman judging his audition from the shadowy corners of the auditorium, along with speech coach Edith Skinner and vocal coach Elizabeth Smith.“John Houseman said from the dark, ‘Do you intend to make acting your profession?’” Kelsey imitates John’s accent with booming gravitas. “I looked at him and I thought, ‘Well, I flew up here from Fort Lauderdale, didn’t I?’ It’s one of my more inspired responses. But they let me in.”Now collaborating on the Rolls-Royce of coffee table books with “The America Opus,” Kelsey reflects on peak Americana with a stunning 50-pound keepsake, or a smaller version better suited to holding in your lap. Considering the foreword from President Donald Trump — and previous comments Kelsey’s made about possibly entering politics later in life — I ask if he’ll be throwing his hat in the ring.“No,” he says. “That’s funny. Well … 2028 would actually probably have to be the time for me, wouldn’t it?” The door remains officially cracked. As for the message of his book, Kelsey muses, “We’ve gotten it right more than we’ve gotten it wrong.”“Countries are full of savage beginnings,” he says, describing America as a reflection of its people. “Its true north has always been the people … a group of individuals that all believe in something special … their future, their creator, their destiny. America is like no other place. It enshrines that right for you to go ahead and figure out what your dream is and do something about it. That’s why I’m here.”Casually aspirational“I’m pretty easygoing, you know, shorts and a T-shirt most of the time at home,” Kelsey confirms when I ask how his off-camera life is different from his public persona. But he and his wife Kayte Walsh may be on the verge of a couple’s makeover.“I’ll show up in public looking semi-decent, but Kayte and I talk about it all the time, like we should dress up more — like Cary Grant,” Kelsey says. “Mostly the white shirt and a nice pair of slacks and a blazer. I do have that as sort of my go-to for public perception.”Still, Kelsey laments a recent foot procedure that had him stuck wearing a surgical boot. “I’ve had a couple of tabloid guys snap a shot while I’m walking in to pick up E. Baldi [Tuscan food], and they’re like, ‘Oh, he looks great.’” I saw the pics. Somehow Kelsey still made post-op look sartorial. Mornings at Kelsey’s house“I tend to wake up early. I usually get up around 5:30,” Kelsey confirms. Taking advantage of a quiet home, he gets right to work. “I’ll do a little writing. I’m working on a memoir, so that’s been going great. But then as soon as the baby wakes up, in he comes and we’re into our morning.”Breakfast might be scrambled eggs depending on the mood, but forget the local coffee shop because the best part of waking up is Kelsey’s perfect cup. “Pretty much every morning I’m the guy that makes the coffees,” he says. “For Kayte, I make an Americano with heavy cream. For myself, I make a breve latte.”Now that he’s mastered his La Marzocco coffee machine, Kelsey says he’s ruined on outside coffee. “I make great coffee,” he says. “It’s gotten to the point where, when I go away, I usually don’t even try to get a cup of coffee.” As for maintaining his fitness into his 70s, Kelsey’s got a guy for that. “I have a Russian kid named Pasha who comes and works me out pretty much every day,” he says. He was linked up with the trainer through Kayte’s brother Phil, who trains professional footballers. “Pasha is an ex-professional soccer player,” Kelsey explains. The actor also admits he’s had “terribly flat feet since I was 8 years old,” but regular physical therapy and a few bionic adjustments have added a bounce to his step. Food on the tableAlong with his four adult children from previous relationships, Kelsey shares four younger children with Kayte. But with their ages ranging from toddler to teen, there’s rarely a consensus on what to eat.“Kayte’s a wonderful cook, but she’s a vegetarian,” Kelsey laughs. “So I do the meat. The boys like hot dogs sometimes, or steak.” But having developed a takeout routine since the lockdowns in Los Angeles, Kelsey says welcoming their youngest only extended the ritual that serves as a quick fix for daily meal planning.“So there’s Faith, Gabriel, James, and now the baby,” Kelsey explains. “We’ll say, ‘Maybe pasta tonight?’ And they’d say, ‘Yeah, but we don’t like penne.’ That’s Faith. Then Gabe doesn’t like tomato sauce with it, and then James says, ‘I’ll eat the star kind.’ So it means we’re cooking three different meals every night. I finally said, ‘Look, one of these days it’s just gonna be whatever your mom’s making that’s what you’re eating, and that’s gonna be it.’”In good companyConsidering he’s got the world at his fingertips, Kelsey’s favorite way to spend time with his family is surprisingly down to earth. “Popcorn and a movie,” he says, sounding legitimately chuffed just thinking about it. “I make the popcorn and then we just put on a movie in the theater.” “James has a sort of encyclopedic knowledge of all animated movies, so we watch a lot of those,” he says. On rare occasions when James lets others weigh in on the feature presentation, the Grammers endure decision fatigue just like every other family. “They say, ‘Nothing out of the nineties … none of those romantic comedies.’”But one classic always makes the cut. “[James’] favorite movie is ‘Ghostbusters,’ and I’m okay with that,” Kelsey says. “What’s even weirder is Gabriel and James’ favorite movie for quite a while was also ‘Jaws.’” Kelsey remembers watching the Spielberg thriller when it came out.“[‘Jaws’] messed me up,” he laughs. “The first time I saw it in the theater in 1975, I actually canceled my diving trip. The next day I called my friend and said, ‘You know, I’m a little busy.’” But Kelsey knew he’d never get over it if he didn’t face his fears. “We went diving two days later, but yeah. That was an effective movie.”The art of living wellAs you might expect, Kelsey studies society’s masterworks on the regular. “I tend to read from all sorts of things all the time,” he says. As for his current nightstand stack, he says, “I’ve been reading ‘Love Letters,’ the A.R. Gurney play. I’m always reading from ‘Paradise Lost.’ I’m always reading bits of the Bible. There’s a great poet named James Merrill who did a wonderful thing called ‘Scripts for the Pageant,’ which I refer to all the time. It’s one of my favorite pieces.”When Kelsey casually tells me “I was reading a little Plato the other day … I’m a real nerd,” I assure him a nerd of his caliber may be better known as a Renaissance man. While he says he doesn’t listen to as much music as he used to, he’s realized somewhat of a lifelong dream.“I recently bought a McIntosh amplifier, which was like a wet dream of an adolescent young man,” he says. “I got a turntable and I have amazing speakers, so I’m listening to vinyl … Frank Sinatra, Seals & Crofts, Todd Rundgren, Leon Russell, some of the classics.” I’m delighted with details that seem so deeply Kelsey Grammer-ish.Straight to the heartLooking back at decades in the business, Kelsey says there’s something Hollywood may be missing now. “Hollywood’s always been sort of a mixture of people with a big agenda that they want to insert into their creativity,” he says. “They’re not telling great stories lately. Honestly, they’ve kind of reduced the size of the human heart.”“Faulkner — when he won the Nobel Prize for Literature — gave some advice to the young writer in his acceptance speech. He said, ‘Whatever you’re writing about, make sure it’s about the human heart, because if it isn’t, it’s about nothing.’ We’ve fallen into doing a lot of nothing,” Kelsey explains. “If I see another movie about a hitman, honestly. Why is treating each other horribly cool or edgy? It doesn’t make a lot of sense to me.
